text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- The Polish Senate Agricultural Committee has supported the proposal to reintroduce customs on grain imports demanded by the lower chamber's Agriculture and Food Economy Commission, the Senate said.
- Over 80 investors, mostly foreign, are ready to invest in the Katowice Special Economic Zone (KSSE).
Total investments in the zone may reach 500 million European Currency Units (ECU) and 10,000 new jobs will be created there, a preliminary forecast by the KSSE management firm said.

- Poland's average net monthly salary in December 1996 was 923.1 zlotys, which showed 7.7 percent growth compared with November and a 25.1 percent increase compared with the same period in 1995, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Germany's Hebel AG concrete maker is planning to enter its products on the Polish market, Hebel's president Rolf-Rudiger Risch said.

- The Starachowice-based Odlewnie Polskie (OPSA) foundry has received an International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9002 quality management certificate from the Berlin-based TUV Cert firm, OPSA president Boguslaw Peczela said.
The company's other two plants in Lodz and Skarzysko Kamienna will receive ISO certificates next year, Peczela said.

- The Polska Zegluga Morska (PZM) shipping firm has contracted the Gdansk Stocznia Remontowa shipyard to reconstruct a 18,500 deadweight tonnage (DWT) bulk carrier and adapt it to liquid sulphur transportation needs, PZM board member Krzysztof Gogol said.
- Over 220 Polish-based paper producers are exhibiting their products at the Wroclaw-based Targopap Zima'97 paper industry fair, which started yesterday.
NOWA EUROPA

- MMC Car Poland, the dealer of Japan's Mitsubishi automaker, sold 400 Dutch-made Carisma passenger cars through a duty free quota last year and plans to double sales this year, MMC Car Poland director Wojciech Szyszko said.
- Poland's advertising market was worth around $604 million in 1996, The European Advertising and Media Forecast said.
Poland stands out as the region's leader in advertising expenditure, which was seen growing a further $1.32 billion by 2000, the forecast said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Korea's Daewoo Corporation has acquired a 60 percent stake in Lublinianka Hotel Lublin, eastern Poland, worth four million zlotys, from Warsaw-based Budimex Trading, which preserved a 40 percent stake in the hotel.
The two firms will carry out Lublinianka's refurbishment, following which the hotel will reach a four star standard.
- Russia has granted Poland a pollock fishing quota of 105,000 tonnes in the Okhotsk Sea, Poland's transport and sea economy ministry's official Zbigniew Graczyk said.
In June Poland plans to renegotiate the size of the quota, Graczyk said.
ZYCIE
- Poland's Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) has accused the urban public road maintenance boards of fund mismanagement , a recent report by NIK said.
- Poland's export revenues from January to November 1996 reached $21.97 billion, a 5.2 percent increase compared with the 1995 results, the National Bank of Poland (NBP), the central bank, said.
PARKIET
- The ZPW Grajewo chipboard maker, to be listed on the Warsaw bourse soon, has presented its development and investment strategy seen doubling the plant's output.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
